newsitem.title: ROMANIA: South Korea Daewoo to open Romania bank.
newsitem.headline: South Korea Daewoo to open Romania bank.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Securities said on Thursday it would open a fully licensed bank in Romania by May, amid plans to develop businesses in the Balkan country.
The new bank's main business will focus on trade, corporate financing and foreign exchange deals related to import and export, the Daewoo Bank (Romania) SA said in a statement.

The bank will start with a share capital of 75 billion lei, with Daewoo Securities holding 89.9 percent, followed by South Korea's KorAm Bank with 10 percent and four Romanian individuals taking the rest of the shares.

The statement also said that in the initial phase the new bank would rely on Daewoo's activities in Romania which include joint ventures with the Craiova-based Automobile Craiova car maker and the Black Sea shipyard of Mangalia.

The bank's future plans include opening four branches across Romania and expanding to deposits and loans, transactions of marketable securities including treasury bonds, securities business services as well as issuing credit cards, it said.
Romania now has some 40 commercial banks, of which 10 are branches of foreign banks.
